# Data

Everything here is derived from the **Eedi dataset released for the NeurIPS 2020
Education Challenge** (Wang et al., 2020). The original question **images are not
redistributed** in this repository — see [Obtaining the images](#obtaining-the-images).

## Files

| File | Rows | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `items.csv` | 725 | The central table. One row per item: `QuestionId`, `image_path`, `difficulty` (Rasch β, the prediction target), `SE_beta`, `n_answers`, `split`, `text` (Q), `visual_description` (D generated by GPT-5.5). |
| `item_manifest.csv` | 725 | The same 725 items and their metadata columns without the `text` / `visual_description` fields — convenient when you only need labels, splits and response counts. |
| `rasch_item_params.csv` | all items | Raw Rasch fit output before any filtering: `item`, `beta`, `SE_beta`. `items.csv` is this table after the deleted-item and ≥200-response filters, joined with response counts and text. |
| `train.csv` / `test.csv` | 580 / 145 | The fixed item-level split. Every system in the paper is trained and evaluated on exactly these. |
| `split_summary.csv` | 2 | Per-split counts and difficulty statistics. |
| `cv_folds.json` | 5 folds | Frozen stratified 5-fold assignment over the 580 training items, used for recipe selection only. Carries a SHA256 of the split so the training scripts can refuse to run against a different split. |
| `question_parsed.json` | 948 | Raw output of the GPT-5.5 parsing pass: `question`, `choices` A–D, `has_figure`, and `figure_description` where applicable. `items.csv` is built from this. |
| `descriptions/*.json` | 401 each | Visual textualizations D produced by five **open** VLMs. Each file records the generating `model`, `family`, `max_new_tokens` and counts, with the text under a `descriptions` object keyed by `QuestionId`. `Qwen_Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct.json` is the D used in the paper's main Q+D results. |

## The two text channels, and why they are different

- **Q** (`text` in `items.csv`) — the question stem and answer choices, extracted from
  the image by GPT-5.5 in a two-pass procedure and then **manually verified**. Treat it
  as a checked image-derived transcription, not as raw OCR and not as ground-truth text
  shipped by Eedi. It deliberately excludes the description of the additional visual
  component. For the 18 items whose answer choices are themselves images, Q contains
  short manually verified descriptions of those choices so the options are not blank.
- **D** (`visual_description`, and `descriptions/*.json`) — a description of the
  *additional visual component only*, generated once from the image and never optimised
  against difficulty labels. 401 of 725 items have one; for the other 324 it is empty and
  Q+D collapses to Q. Unlike Q, D is **not** manually verified — it is the experimental
  variable.

## Labels

`difficulty` is the item parameter β of a one-parameter logistic (Rasch) model fitted to
the released student correctness records, P(correct) = σ(θ_u − β_i). Larger β = harder.
Items marked deleted in the Eedi metadata and items with fewer than 200 observed
responses were removed, leaving 725. Retained β values span roughly −2.91 to 1.96, with a
median of 2,155 responses per item (range 203–2,966) and reported standard errors of mean
0.061 / median 0.054 / range 0.043–0.162.

This is a psychometric estimate from student responses, **not** a human-annotated
difficulty rating and not a field in the Eedi metadata.

## Obtaining the images

The Eedi question images are part of the NeurIPS 2020 Education Challenge release and are
not included here. Download that release yourself, then point the code at the image
directory:

```bash
export VDIFF_IMAGES=/path/to/eedi/images
```

`image_path` in `items.csv` is `images/<QuestionId>.jpg`; only the basename is used, so
any flat directory of `<QuestionId>.jpg` files will work. `QuestionId` is the challenge's
own identifier, so the join back to the original release is exact.

The text-only routes (Q and Q+D) run **without** the images. Only the image-native
routes (`vlm_lora_regression.py`, `generate_descriptions.py`,
`eval_image_intervention.py`) need them.

## Rebuilding from source

```bash
python src/prepare/parse_questions.py            # images -> question_parsed.json (needs an OpenAI key)
python src/prepare/clean_newlines.py
python src/prepare/prepare_difficulty_dataset.py # Rasch fit + filtering + split -> items.csv
python src/make_cv_folds.py                      # -> cv_folds.json
```

## Licensing

The Rasch parameters, splits, folds, and predictions in this repository are our own
output. The Q transcriptions and D descriptions are **derived from the Eedi item
images**; if you redistribute them, check the terms of the original Eedi / NeurIPS 2020
Education Challenge release, which govern the underlying content.
